# Air Traffic Control careers
## The role of   Air Traffic Controller
As an Air Traffic Controller, you will be playing a crucial role as the guardian of the Australian sky. You will be part of a vital team that manages 11% of the world’s airspace, and guided by world-class technology will ensure the safe, reliable and efficient airspace use of all aircraft operating in our skies.

Lauren - Air Traffic Controller | Full version - YouTube

[Lauren - Air Traffic Controller | Full version](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=dhcN1nKeRKc) [Airservices Australia](https://www.youtube.com/channel/UC7PuoYiezAXHtVR_s0XWRzA)

## World-class training
#### Role details
- been employed as an operational air traffic controller within the last five years AND been employed within an air traffic control field such as instructing during the remaining time.

## Air Traffic Control Trainee   Meet Adam Hart
He is studying to become an enroute air traffic controller and is undergoing 14 months of training to gain his qualification as a guardian of the Australian sky.

He is studying to become an enroute air traffic controller and is undergoing 14 months of training to gain his qualification as a guardian of the Australian sky.

(air traffic controller over radio)

This is easily the most challenging thing I've done and once I've finished that and become an air traffic controller, it'll be the most rewarding experience I've ever encountered.

An air traffic controller working in a tower at [Zurich International Airport](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zurich_International_Airport), Switzerland. Air traffic controller An **air traffic controller** ( **ATC**) is a person responsible for the coordination of air traffic within [controlled airspace](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Controlled_airspace). ## History ### Origins [[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Air_traffic_controller#cite_note-4) In the US, [Archie League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Archie_League) is regarded as the first air traffic controller and was hired by the city of [St. Louis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._Louis) in 1929 to prevent collisions. ## Roles ### Civilian/military [![](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/6/6d/US_Navy_060505-N-9079D-025_Air_Traffic_Controller_3rd_Class_David_McKeehe_works_approach_controller_in_Carrier_Air_Traffic_Control_Center_%28CATTC%29.jpg/250px-US_Navy_060505-N-9079D-025_Air_Traffic_Controller_3rd_Class_David_McKeehe_works_approach_controller_in_Carrier_Air_Traffic_Control_Center_%28CATTC%29.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:US_Navy_060505-N-9079D-025_Air_Traffic_Controller_3rd_Class_David_McKeehe_works_approach_controller_in_Carrier_Air_Traffic_Control_Center_(CATTC).jpg) A military air traffic controller at approach control on the [USS _Abraham Lincoln_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USS_Abraham_Lincoln_(CVN-72)) (CVN-72). [[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Air_traffic_controller#cite_note-j099-28) In some countries all air traffic controlling is handled by the military and all controllers are soldiers. ## References 56.
